The excursion begins in São Paulo's historic centre. The route includes Praça da Sé and the cathedral, the Japanese quarter, the city's founding square, the Viaduto do Chá and the Municipal Theatre of Opera and Ballet. You will then see the square by the railway station, the Municipal Market, Praça da República and the Edifício Itália, also known as the "Italian Terrace".

Next, you will discover the modern side of the city. Paulista Avenue gives way to the green paths, lakes and canals of Ibirapuera Park. The park has playgrounds and cycle paths. Here you can see the Obelisk commemorating those who took part in the 1932 revolution and the Monument to the Bandeiras, dedicated to expeditions into Brazil's interior.

To finish, you will see neighbourhoods with modern architecture and visit the graffiti district. The excursion is guided; its duration and the language of the guide are agreed at the time of booking.

Today you will discover another side of São Paulo: a little calmer and more reflective, as though the city has slowed its frantic pace for a moment to reveal chapters of its own history.

We will set out for the historic centre, where the colonial past comes alive in old buildings, grand cathedrals and atmospheric squares. Here, among stone-paved streets and intricately decorated altars, the city's story gradually unfolds, from its earliest days to its transformation into one of the world's largest metropolises. Every façade, every square and every architectural detail holds memories of the events and people that shaped São Paulo.

Today you will do more than admire the sights: it will feel as though you have travelled through time, touching the city's past, which still lives on in its streets.

The excursion begins in Ibirapuera Park, the city's main green space. Here you will learn about the historical significance of the Obelisk and the Monument to the Bandeiras and see works by the famous Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer, including the Museum of Contemporary Art (MAC) and the Oca pavilion.

The route then continues through the elegant Jardins district, where you can admire well-known landmarks such as the unusual architecture of the Hotel Unique and the traditional Nossa Senhora do Brasil Church.

Next, you will head to Vila Madalena, a neighbourhood known for its creative, bohemian atmosphere. It is home to the famous Beco do Batman, a picturesque alley covered in colourful graffiti and murals that change constantly.

The tour then follows the legendary Paulista Avenue, one of the city's principal thoroughfares, before continuing to São Paulo's historic centre.

You will see the celebrated Copan and Itália buildings, the Anhangabaú Valley, the Municipal Theatre, City Hall, the historic Pátio do Colégio complex, the São Bento Monastery and São Paulo's magnificent Metropolitan Cathedral on Praça da Sé.

Immerse yourself in the fast-moving pace of a city that seems never to stop. Accompanied by a local guide, you will explore São Paulo, a city of striking contrasts where gleaming skyscrapers stand beside historic façades and contemporary life is woven into the heritage of earlier eras.

You will walk along the city's famous streets and avenues, experience the distinctive atmosphere of Paulista Avenue and discover how the city's energy is reflected in every intersection, neighbourhood and movement.

São Paulo is more than Brazil's largest metropolis. It is the country's cultural and business heart, a city that lives at its own rapid pace and reveals a new facet of its many-sided personality every day.

In a traditional boat, you cross Canaima Lagoon and head towards Hacha and Sapo waterfalls. The excursion includes a passage behind a wall of water: the torrent falls directly in front of you, with the rock close beside you. Here, the roar of falling water and the flying spray are especially vivid.

After the excursion, you return to the lodge. Access to individual sections of the waterfalls depends on water levels and the weather; guides lead the route on site.
